subject: Weekly pipeline-to-GPU scenario workback — runway, burst & pre-close contingencies
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Orion weekly: ask for runway numbers + gating for pre-close burst

Mina / team —

Following up from the pipeline readout: Orion's Q3 close is looking like a multi-stage roll (pilot -> parallel production). They asked for a hard pre-close burst window for their pilot a week before contract signature (to demo load at scale). Need to align on reserve exposure and a backup plan we can trigger automatically.

Can infra confirm the answers to these by EOD today so I can update Sarah and procurement:
- If we commit a 2-week burst of 50 A100-equivalent slots, what is the impact to existing reserved pool (expected slug across May-July)?
- What fallback capacity can we promise (e.g., lower-precision model variant, 50% tokens) and what SLO hit does that produce?
- Estimated incremental cost range (low/med/high) for the burst request.

I attached a cleaned scenario sheet (v2) with our assumptions and suggested tranche sizes. I'll be on the 11:30 sales call; can we table final numbers there?

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orion_scenario_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Leung <sarah@orion-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orion weekly: ask for runway numbers + gating for pre-close burst

Jordan — good framing. Quick notes from product/ops side before infra math:
- We should treat the pre-close burst as "guaranteed best-effort" unless procurement signs a short-term reserve addendum. That means we can do scheduling priority but not hard SLAs beyond the Dedicated pool SLA.
- Recommend we prepare two supported fallbacks to present to Orion: (1) quantized model variant with identical API (lower latency/cost), (2) token-throttling policy with transparent degradation profile.

Ben / Laura — please fill in the numeric answers below; I need a conservative and an optimistic runway so sales and finance can model ARR uplift vs hardware exposure.

Deliverables (for 16:30 internal sync):
- Conservative: capacity draw + worst-case latency degradation + monthly cost delta
- Optimistic: minimal disrupt plan + cost delta + lead-time to provision additional reserved slots
- Short-form copy for procurement that outlines the tradeoffs (we'll need this for contract redlines)

Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Sales Ops (on capacity)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Orion weekly: ask for runway numbers + gating for pre-close burst

Mina / Jordan —

Quick calc based on current pool and expected Q3 commitments (high-level):
- Current reserved pool: 1,200 A100-equivalent slot-hours/day averaged across accounts (baseline).
- Committed runway (existing reserves + near-term): ~1,450 slot-hours/day.
- Requested burst: 50 A100 slots for 14 days -> ~700 slot-hours/day added during that window (peak).

Conservative impact (assume no extra provisioning): we'd need to divert ~48% of burst demand to shared burst queue, which has lower priority. That would increase average token latency by ~25-35% for affected requests; tail latency could worsen more during peak. Cost uplift estimate (rounded):
- Low: $38k (if we utilize existing burst credits and autoscaling efficiencies)
- Mid: $62k (mix of reserved burst + spot GPU hours)
- High: $95k (if we provision short-term reserved capacity in additional regions to avoid contention)

Optimistic path (if we provision 100 additional reserved slots for the quarter):
- Lead time to provision: ~7 business days if capacity available in region; 14+ days if procurement + rack ordering required.
- Latency impact: <10% on average with quota controls and priority routing.
- Cost delta: +$48k (amortized across quarter).

Attachments: I uploaded a short scenario worksheet (orion_scenario_v2.xlsx) with the line-item math and cost buckets. Also attached a reserve_request_form.pdf to start procurement if we decide to pursue the optimistic path.

Ben Carter
Lead, Fleet Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orion weekly: ask for runway numbers + gating for pre-close burst

Thanks Ben — +1 to the numbers, and a couple of operational notes from provisioning:

Operational constraints and recommended playbook:
1) If Orion signs a short-term reserved addendum we can greenlight the 100-slot optimistic path immediately; legal/procurement should target a 7 business day turnaround.
2) If addendum is not signed, use the burst credits + priority routing with these controls:
   - Apply model-variant flag so pilot traffic is placed on quantized variant automatically during peak windows.
   - Enable prefix KV caching for demo datasets to reduce token load by ~20-30%.
   - Implement a soft rate limit per-API-key that gracefully degrades after X requests/minute (we'll provide suggested thresholds).
3) Finance: recommend we present the three cost buckets Ben outlined and propose a shared risk credit (5-10% credit) if we provide the burst before signature — helps close probability.

Action items for 16:30 internal sync:
- Ben: confirm line-item math in the sheet + finalize the conservative and optimistic cells
- Jordan: prepare short procurement note for Orion (I can edit) and confirm whether Sarah can accept a 7-day reserved addendum in principle
- Mina: I'll draft the short-form ops playbook (1 page) so procurement & legal have a clear list of operational constraints to own in the contract

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
